messages:
Sam: Quick idea — instead of shipping language-specific parsers for continuation tokens, keep tokens opaque and provide a very small cross-lang adapter that handles handshake, resume semantics, and optimistic prefetch. saves duplication and keeps runtime decoupled.
Mona: Sounds promising. how do we handle retries/idempotency? if client retries with an old token are we safe? :thinking_face:
Julian: Python iterators make this tricky — users expect a simple for-loop. If we expose a helper it should implement __iter__/__next__ and hide retry backoff. otherwise we push complexity onto app devs.
Keiko: TS can use async iterators + a tiny helper like `continuationAdapter(streamFn, token)` that returns an `AsyncIterable`. ergonomic.
Ash: Concern: streaming transports (gRPC/WS) vs unary/polling endpoints behave differently. adapter must not assume streaming semantics or it will leak transport details to SDKs.
Mona: Proposal: an adapter interface with three primitives: `start(token?) -> sessionHandle`, `next(sessionHandle) -> {items, continuation?, stateMeta}`, `close(sessionHandle)`. Transport impls provide the `start/next/close` wiring. language SDKs provide the iterator wrapper that implements idiomatic APIs.
Sam: Example usage sketch (TS):
```ts
const it = continuationAdapter(({start, next}) => ({
  start: () => api.post('/list', {token}),
  next: (cursor) => api.get(`/list?page=${cursor}`)
}), initialToken);
for await (const item of it) { /* ... */ }
```
Mona: Also include a request-id + client-nonce in headers so server can detect duplicate commit windows. header names: `x-rw-client-id`, `x-rw-nonce`.
Julian: We should version tokens to avoid us having to decode them. server includes `v:2` in token payload. Adapter treats token as opaque string; server guarantees forward/back compat.
Keiko: For Python/TS we export the same adapter name and options: `max_retries`, `prefetch`, `on_progress` callback. For Go we expose a channel + helper that converts adapter into `chan Item`. Keep API surface minimal.
Ash: One more: fallback behavior when the token is incompatible (server returns 400/410). adapter should surface a `ResetError` that lets user decide to restart from scratch or abort. default: raise and log.
ops-bot: Reminder: RFC link added to thread: <https://redwood.rfc/internal/continuations>. follow-up meeting Friday 10am.
Sam: Action items: (1) Julian + Keiko implement PoC for Python/TS adapter (2 weeks), (2) Ash to write compatibility tests for transport flavors, (3) Mona to update server token doc to include `v` and headers.
Mona: +1, I can draft the server token doc and add examples for `x-rw-client-id`.
Julian: I'll start the Python iterator wrapper tomorrow and post a tiny prototype in this thread.
Keiko: I'll mirror in TS and wire an async-iterable test.
Ash: I'll add a small suite for grpc/http/polling combinations.
Sam: Nice. keeping tokens opaque + a tiny adapter feels like the right balance between ergonomics and transport isolation. :thumbsup:
